a04-turbine-count.answer: The updated application covers 46 natural gas-fired turbines: two combined cycle turbines and 44 simple cycle turbines.[1] These are 2 GE 7HA.02 combined-cycle turbines, 3 GE 7HA.02 simple-cycle turbines, 12 Solar Titan 350 simple-cycle turbines and 29 Solar Titan 130 simple-cycle turbines.[1] The original application filed in October 2025 proposed 17 combustion turbines.[2] The 29 Solar T130 turbines were added in an update on December 22, 2025, to supply 'early phase power' and are not intended to stay onsite long-term.[1][3]

a02-capacity-original.answer: The original application filed in October 2025 stated that the Kilby site's nominal power generation capacity would be approximately 2,595 megawatts (MW).[1] That original application covered two combined-cycle turbines and fifteen simple-cycle turbines, along with other equipment.[1] The figure changed later: in the December 22, 2025 response to a deficiency notice, the company gave 2,476 MW at defined site conditions for those turbines and proposed adding 29 early-phase turbines of approximately 393 MW.[2] TCEQ's later review summary, dated April 10, 2026, lists the plant's capacity as approximately 2,869 MW.[3]

a03-capacity-chevron.answer: Chevron announced that Project Kilby is expected to deliver approximately 2.67 gigawatts of capacity, built through a phased, modular approach that allows incremental expansion over time.[1] Chevron said most of that generation will come from large GE Vernova turbines, with additional capacity from Solar Turbines.[1] This figure differs from the state air permit file, which puts the plant's nominal capacity at approximately 2,869 megawatts across 46 turbines.[2] The permit figure has also changed over time: the October 2025 application stated approximately 2,595 MW, and 29 turbines were added in a December 22, 2025 update.[3][2] One analysis treats 2.67 GW as the commercial project scale and 2.869 GW as the permit envelope.[4]

a01-capacity-permit.answer: The most recent figure in the TCEQ permit file puts the Kilby Power Plant's nominal generating capacity at approximately 2,869 megawatts (MW), measured at site conditions of 59°F, 60% relative humidity and 2,850 feet elevation.[1] That figure covers 46 turbines, including 29 Solar Titan 130 units that were added in a December 22, 2025 update to supply 'early phase power.'[1] The original application, filed in October 2025, gave a lower capacity of approximately 2,595 MW.[2] In its December 22, 2025 response to TCEQ, the company restated the output of the original turbines as 2,476 MW at site conditions and said the 29 added early-phase turbines would provide approximately 393 MW.[3] A company press release from Joulent (not part of the permit file) gives a different figure of approximately 2.67 gigawatts.[4]

a06-7ha-rating.answer: Each of the two GE 7HA.02 combined-cycle turbines at the Kilby Power Plant has a net output of 555.7 MW.[1][2] The same figure appears in Energy Forge One's December 22, 2025 response to TCEQ, which gives it at site conditions of 59°F inlet air temperature, 60% relative humidity, and 2,850 feet elevation.[3]

a05-t130-purpose.answer: According to the TCEQ permit file, the 29 Solar Titan 130 simple-cycle turbines are proposed to supply 'early phase power' to meet customer needs and are not intended to stay onsite long-term.[1] They were added to the project scope in an update to the application on December 22, 2025; the original October 2025 application listed only 17 turbines (2 combined-cycle GE 7HA.02, 3 simple-cycle GE 7HA.02 and 12 Solar Titan 350).[1][2] An analyst brief (tier 4) likewise describes the roughly 393 MW Titan 130 fleet as temporary early power and a bridge fleet that can protect the schedule, but says it needs a hard replacement milestone.[3][4]

a07-ppa-term.answer: The power purchase agreement for Project Kilby runs for 20 years, under which Energy Forge One LLC, a Chevron subsidiary, will supply dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center.[1] Chevron announced the agreement on June 22, 2026.[1] Other sources, including Joulent and press coverage, consistently describe the same 20-year term.[2][3]

a08-offtaker.answer: Microsoft will buy the power from Project Kilby under a 20-year power purchase agreement.[1][2] The plant will provide dedicated electricity to a Microsoft-operated data center that is co-located with the facility in West Texas.[1] The agreement is with Energy Forge One, a Chevron subsidiary, and the plant is expected to deliver about 2.67 gigawatts.[3]

a10-county.answer: The Kilby Power Plant is in Reeves County, Texas, near Pecos, according to the TCEQ notice of application for its air quality permits.[1] The applicant's air dispersion modeling protocol likewise compares the Project Kilby site's area to Reeves County when justifying its choice of monitors.[2]

a09-applicant.answer: Energy Forge One LLC applied to the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality for the Kilby air permits, numbered 181895, PSDTX1684 and GHGPSDTX260.[1][2] The application was submitted to the TCEQ on October 17, 2025.[1] The TCEQ's summary form describes the request as an air construction permit for a greenfield natural gas-fired turbine power plant near Pecos, Reeves County, Texas.[3]

a11-substation.answer: In the ERCOT interconnection queue, the Energy Forge One LLC (Kilby1) projects in Reeves County list their point of interconnection as the Solstice Substation at 345 kV.[1] This same POI appears for all four Kilby1 entries (Parts 1, 2, 4 and 6) in both the August 2026 and October 2026 reports.[2][1] The "Kilby Station" and "Kilby Switching Station" entries in the same reports belong to the unrelated Quantum Solar and Quantum Storage projects in Haskell County, not to Project Kilby.[1]

a13-part1-cod.answer: ERCOT's October 2026 interconnection status report lists a projected commercial operation date of 2027-11-04 for Kilby1 Part 1 Small Block Simple Cycle (INR 27INR0572).[1] That project is a 371 MW gas turbine project by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County, and the report shows it had no interconnection agreement yet ("SS Completed, FIS Started, No IA").[1]

a12-battery-now.answer: In the October 2026 ERCOT interconnection report, the battery storage portion of Project Kilby is listed as "Kilby1 Part 2 Tier1 BESS" with a capacity of 330 MW.[1] It is filed by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County, with a projected commercial operation date of 2028-01-21.[1] The earlier August 2026 report showed the same 330 MW figure.[2] The "Quantum Storage" battery in the same report is a separate project in Haskell County at the unrelated Kilby Switching Station, not part of Project Kilby.[1]

a14-first-power.answer: Chevron says first power delivery from Project Kilby is anticipated in 2028.[1] That timing held as of October 2026: even though Chevron's final investment decision could slip to 2027 because of a moratorium on new data center permits, Chevron's vice president for power solutions said Kilby is still on track to produce first electrons by 2028.[2] Partner and press sources give the same target of first power by 2028.[3] ERCOT's October 2026 interconnection report lists a projected commercial operation date of 2027-11-04 for the first Kilby gas block, Part 1.[4]

a15-fid-timing.answer: In its June 22, 2026 announcement, Chevron said its Final Investment Decision (FID) on Kilby was expected by the end of 2026, subject to the completion of other necessary conditions.[1][2] National Grid's July 2026 description of the project also gave a final investment decision expected in 2026.[3][4] However, Semafor reported on October 1, 2026 that the decision could be pushed to 2027 after Gov. Greg Abbott imposed a moratorium on new data center permits, citing Chevron's vice president for power solutions, Daniel Droog.[5] Droog said Kilby was still on track to produce its first electrons by 2028.[5]

a16-co2e-updated.answer: In the TCEQ permit file at technical completeness, the proposed allowable emission rate for greenhouse gases is 13,890,275.01 tons per year as CO2e, including 13,871,124.49 tons per year of CO2.[1] That same file describes the project as 46 turbines, after 29 Solar Titan 130 turbines were added in an update on December 22, 2025.[2] For comparison, the original plain language summary, filed with the 17-turbine application in October 2025, listed 11,564,704.59 tons per year of CO2 equivalent.[3][4]

a17-co2e-pls.answer: A draft answer failed the page check, so it is not shown.

a19-water.answer: Chevron says the Kilby plant plans to use non-potable, brackish groundwater rather than freshwater for power plant operations.[1] Chevron also says it is working on ways to reuse produced water from oil and gas operations.[1] An independent analysis likewise describes closed-loop campus cooling and nonpotable or brackish sources as proposed, but notes that initial fill, construction water and water rights still need confirmation.[2]

a20-filed-date.answer: Energy Forge One LLC submitted the Kilby air permit application (Permit 181895, PSDTX1684 and GHGPSDTX260) to TCEQ on October 17, 2025.[1] TCEQ's pending permit list shows the same date, 10/17/2025, for the Kilby application.[2][3] The application was later updated on December 22, 2025, when 29 turbines were added to the project scope.[4]

a21-public-meeting.answer: The TCEQ public meeting on the Kilby permit application was scheduled for Wednesday, June 10, 2026 at 7:00 PM.[1] The venue was the Reeves County Civic Center, 1500 S Cedar Street, Pecos, Texas 79772.[1] The meeting was to have two parts, an Informal Discussion Period and a Formal Comment Period, and the notice announcing it was issued on May 5, 2026.[1] The provided pages are the meeting notice itself, so they show when and where the meeting was scheduled but do not confirm that it actually took place as planned.[1]

a18-nox-controls.answer: NOx from the proposed natural gas turbines will be controlled by selective catalytic reduction (SCR), while an oxidation catalyst handles CO and VOC.[1] SCR uses ammonia as a reducing agent to convert NOx to water and nitrogen, and the ammonia injection rate is controlled to avoid both too little NOx reduction and unwanted ammonia slip.[2] For the combined-cycle 7HA turbines, the proposed ammonia slip limit is 5 ppmvd at 15% O2.[2] The simple-cycle turbine NOx analysis also lists Dry Low-NOx (DLN) burners, which are built into the turbine design and are proposed to be used together with SCR.[3] An alternative, the EMx/SCONOx catalytic absorption system, was rejected as technically infeasible for large turbines.[3]

a22-permit-number.answer: The state air quality permit number for Project Kilby is 181895, which Energy Forge One LLC applied for alongside federal PSD permit PSDTX1684 and greenhouse gas PSD permit GHGPSDTX260.[1] The application was submitted to the TCEQ on October 17, 2025.[1] The same three numbers appear on the TCEQ pending permit list for the Kilby site.[2]

a24-national-grid.answer: National Grid, through its National Grid Ventures arm, agreed to invest $1.75 billion in Joulent, which Joulent described as a strategic minority investment.[1] Press reports say the investment bought a 35% stake in Joulent.[2][3] Joulent's own announcement, dated July 1, 2026, does not state the stake percentage.[1]

a26-technically-complete.answer: The pages do not show any date on which TCEQ estimated the application would be technically complete. The TCEQ pending permit list shows the Kilby application (181895, GHGPSDTX260, PSDTX1684) with a date of 10/17/2025. Its status was 'Administrative Complete Application' in the 2026-04-10 snapshot and 'Technically Complete Application' in the 2026-10-30 snapshot. The permit file at technical completeness is dated 2026-08-06. None of these pages gives a projected or estimated completion date.

a23-suppliers.answer: A draft answer failed the page check, so it is not shown.

a25-final-issuance-estimate.answer: A TCEQ RBLC summary form for the Kilby Power Plant, dated April 10, 2026 and prepared by reviewer Huy Pham, gives an estimated final issuance date of 10/15/2026.[1] The same form estimated the PN2 and technically complete date as 4/15/2026.[1] A later snapshot of TCEQ's pending permit list still shows the Kilby application with the status "Technically Complete Application."[2]

c01-battery-change.answer: Between the two ERCOT interconnection reports provided, the size of Project Kilby's battery storage entry did not change: it was listed at 330 MW in the August 2026 report.[1] The October 2026 report shows the same battery entry, Kilby1 Part 2 Tier1 BESS, still at 330 MW, with the same projected commercial operation date of 2028-01-21.[2] The "Quantum Storage" battery project in the same reports, at 321.75 MW, is a separate Haskell County project at the unrelated Kilby Switching Station, not part of Project Kilby.[2]

c03-turbine-change.answer: The original application, dated October 2025, proposed 17 combustion turbines: 2 GE 7HA.02 combined-cycle turbines, 3 GE 7HA.02 simple-cycle turbines and 12 Solar Titan 350 simple-cycle turbines.[1] In the update to the application, Energy Forge One proposed adding 29 simple cycle turbines to supply approximately 393 MW of early phase power to meet customer needs.[2] The TCEQ review summary states that these 29 Solar T130 turbines were added on December 22, 2025, and that they are not intended to stay onsite long-term.[3] After the update, the project consists of 46 turbines: 2 combined cycle turbines and 44 simple cycle turbines.[3]

c02-capacity-change.answer: The original application, dated October 2025, put the Kilby site's nominal capacity at approximately 2,595 MW, from two combined-cycle and fifteen simple-cycle natural gas turbines.[1] In its December 22, 2025 response to TCEQ's deficiency notice, the company restated the output of those original turbines as 2,476 MW at defined site conditions, which differs from the 2,595 MW in the original filing.[2] The same update proposed adding 29 simple-cycle turbines for early-phase power, with a nominal net output of approximately 393 MW.[2] TCEQ's April 10, 2026 review summary describes the updated project as 46 turbines with a nominal capacity of approximately 2,869 MW. It notes that the 29 Solar T130 turbines were added in the December 22, 2025 update.[3]

u01-turbine-cost.answer: The provided pages do not state how much the GE Vernova turbines cost. They describe the turbine models (GE 7HA.02 units) and note that Engine No. 1's founder procured four gigawatts of GE Vernova gas turbines, but they give no purchase price. The only dollar figures are National Grid Ventures' $1.75 billion investment in Joulent and a headline link mentioning a '$7B Texas power plant,' and neither is a turbine cost.

c06-part6-technology.answer: Yes, the technology code listed for Kilby1 Part 6 Large Block Combined Cycle (INR 29INR0199) differs between the two ERCOT reports.[1][2] In the August 2026 report (published 2026-09-01), the technology was listed as CC.[1] In the October 2026 report (published 2026-11-02), the technology was listed as GT.[2] Other listed details for this project, such as the 1056 MW capacity and the 2029-07-19 projected COD, are the same in both reports, and the pages do not explain why the technology code changed.[2][1]

u02-epc-contractor.answer: The provided pages do not name the EPC contractor for the Kilby Power Plant. The permit application only refers generically to 'the Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) contractor', which will run the commissioning phase before handing control to EFO. A Latitude Media article (published 2026-07-10) reports that Joulent hadn't announced its EPC contractor for Kilby yet and was finalizing a contract with 'a brand name'.

u05-acreage.answer: The provided pages do not state the acreage of the Kilby site. They give its location in Reeves County, about 20 miles south of Pecos, and note that the area map shows 3,000 feet from the property line, but no acreage figure appears.

u03-construction-cost.answer: None of the provided pages states the total construction cost of the Kilby power plant. The TCEQ file (P1) estimates a project total cost for carbon capture of 11972 $Million, but that figure is for a hypothetical carbon capture system, not for building the plant. The press page (P5) includes a related-article headline, 'Chevron eyes $7B Texas power plant for Microsoft data center campus', but it is only a link title and does not itself state a cost for Project Kilby.

u04-ppa-price.answer: The provided pages describe a 20-year power purchase agreement between Energy Forge One LLC (Chevron) and Microsoft for about 2.67 GW. None of them disclose the price per MWh Microsoft will pay. Chevron says only that the project is targeting mid-teen returns. The Frontier Grid brief models fuel commodity price cases per MMBtu, which are analytical assumptions and not PPA terms.

c05-solar-fate.answer: None of the Project Kilby queue entries filed by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County is a solar project; the entries are gas turbine and battery storage blocks.[1] The solar entry that mentions "Kilby" is Quantum Solar, a separate Haskell County project by IP QUANTUM II, LLC that connects at Kilby Station, so it is not part of Project Kilby.[1] For that unrelated Quantum Solar project, the projected commercial operation date was 2026-09-01 in the August 2026 report and 2026-11-30 in the October 2026 report.[2][1] In Project Kilby's air permit file, "Solar" refers to Solar Titan 350 gas-fired combustion turbines, not solar power.[3]

u07-mercuria.answer: The provided pages do not mention a Pecos Power Plant built by Mercuria or a Texas Energy Fund loan. They cover only Project Kilby (Energy Forge One LLC, Chevron), which is a different project, so its megawatt figures cannot be used to answer this question.

u06-lcoe.answer: None of the provided pages gives a levelized cost of electricity for the Kilby Power Plant. The pages do include a cost estimate for carbon capture: a final figure of $194/ton of CO2 removed, along with capital and operating costs for capture trains. They also say Chevron's Permian gas gives the project a cost advantage. However, no per-MWh cost of electricity is stated.

u08-engine-no1-price.answer: The provided pages do not say that Chevron paid Engine No. 1 anything for a share of Project Kilby. They describe Kilby as a collaboration and a 50-50 joint venture between Chevron and Joulent, which spun out of Engine No. 1. The only investment figure given is a separate deal: National Grid Ventures' $1.75 billion investment in Joulent for a 35% stake in that company. None of the pages give a price paid by Chevron.

u10-revenue.answer: The provided pages do not state how much annual revenue Project Kilby will earn from Microsoft. They describe a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft for about 2.67 gigawatts and say the project is "targeting mid-teen returns," but they give no dollar figure for annual revenue or for the contract price.

u09-dc-contractor.answer: The provided pages do not name a general contractor for Microsoft's Pecos data center. They only discuss the power plant's EPC contractor. Latitude Media (July 10, 2026) says Joulent had not yet announced the EPC contractor for Kilby but was finalizing a contract with "a brand name." National Grid, as cited in the Frontier Grid brief, says EPC capacity is reserved. Neither source identifies a contractor for the data center itself.

a14-first-power.answer: Chevron says first power delivery from Project Kilby is anticipated in 2028.[1] In an October 2026 interview, Chevron's Daniel Droog said Kilby was still on track to produce its first electrons by 2028, even though the final investment decision could slip to 2027 because of a moratorium on new data center permits.[2] National Grid's investment announcement gives the same target, saying the project is targeting first power delivery by 2028.[3] ERCOT's October 2026 interconnection report lists an earlier projected commercial operation date of 2027-11-04 for the first Kilby block, a 371 MW simple cycle unit.[4]

a12-battery-now.answer: In the October 2026 ERCOT interconnection status report, the battery storage portion of Project Kilby is listed as "Kilby1 Part 2 Tier1 BESS" (INR 28INR0457) with a capacity of 330 MW.[1] It is filed by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County, with a projected commercial operation date of 2028-01-21, and its study phase is "SS Completed, FIS Started, No IA."[1] The August 2026 report showed the same 330 MW figure.[2] The 321.75 MW "Quantum Storage" battery in the same report belongs to a separate Haskell County project at Kilby Switching Station, not Project Kilby.[1]

a11-substation.answer: In ERCOT's October interconnection status report, all four Energy Forge One LLC "Kilby1" entries in Reeves County list the #60404 Solstice Substation at 345 kV as the point of interconnection.[1] The earlier May report differs for Kilby1 Part 1 (Small Block Simple Cycle), which was listed as a double tap of the 345kV Parker (1436) - Benbrook (1873 & 1869) circuit rather than Solstice.[2] In that May report, the other Kilby1 parts were already listed at the #60404 Solstice Substation 345 kV.[2] The "60089 Kilby Station 345kV" that appears in the same reports belongs to the unrelated Quantum Solar and Quantum Storage projects in Haskell County, not to Project Kilby.[1]

a15-fid-timing.answer: In its June 22, 2026 announcement, Chevron said its Final Investment Decision (FID) on Project Kilby was expected by the end of 2026, subject to completing other necessary conditions.[1] In July 2026, National Grid's investment coverage and an analysis brief also described FID as expected in 2026.[2][3] A later Semafor report dated October 1, 2026 says the decision could slip to 2027 after Gov. Greg Abbott imposed a moratorium on new data center permits.[4] Semafor attributes this to Daniel Droog, Chevron's vice president for power solutions, who also said Kilby is still on track to produce its first electrons by 2028.[4]

a19-water.answer: According to Chevron, the Kilby plant plans to use non-potable, brackish groundwater rather than freshwater for power plant operations.[1] Chevron also says it is working on ways to reuse produced water from oil and gas operations.[1] An analyst brief similarly describes closed-loop campus cooling and nonpotable or brackish sources as proposed, but notes that initial fill, construction water and water rights still require confirmation.[2]

a21-public-meeting.answer: The TCEQ public meeting on the Kilby Power Plant air permit application was scheduled for Wednesday, June 10, 2026 at 7:00 PM.[1] It was to be held at the Reeves County Civic Center, 1500 S Cedar Street, Pecos, Texas 79772.[1] The notice announcing the meeting was issued on May 5, 2026, and the meeting was to have two parts: an Informal Discussion Period and a Formal Comment Period.[1] The provided pages give the scheduled date and location but do not confirm that the meeting actually took place as planned.[1]

a22-permit-number.answer: The state air quality permit number for the Kilby Power Plant is 181895, which Energy Forge One LLC applied for alongside federal Prevention of Significant Deterioration permit PSDTX1684 and greenhouse gas PSD permit GHGPSDTX260.[1] The TCEQ pending permit list shows the same three numbers, with an application date of 10/17/2025.[2] Note that one TCEQ summary form lists the greenhouse gas number as "GHGPSDTX260181895", which appears to run two numbers together; other filings give it as GHGPSDTX260.[3][4]

a24-national-grid.answer: National Grid, through its National Grid Ventures arm, agreed to invest $1.75 billion in Joulent, according to Joulent's July 1, 2026 announcement, which describes it as a strategic minority investment.[1] Press reports say the $1.75 billion bought a 35% stake in Joulent.[2][3] Joulent is developing Project Kilby through a 50-50 joint venture with Chevron.[3]

a23-suppliers.answer: The permit file lists turbines from two makers: GE 7HA.02 units and Solar Titan units.[1] Five of the turbines are GE 7HA.02 models: 2 run in combined-cycle mode and 3 run in simple-cycle mode.[1] The rest are Solar models: 12 Solar Titan 350 units and 29 Solar Titan 130 units, all simple-cycle.[1] The original October 2025 application listed only 17 turbines (the GE units and the 12 Solar T350s), and the 29 Solar T130 units were added in an update on December 22, 2025.[2][1] The pages identify these turbines by model name but do not describe any purchase or supply contract with either manufacturer.[3]

a26-technically-complete.answer: TCEQ's RBLC summary form for Project Kilby, dated April 10, 2026, gave an estimated technically complete date of 4/15/2026.[1] The same form estimated final issuance for 10/15/2026.[1] TCEQ's pending permit list showed the Kilby application as "Administrative Complete Application" in an April 10, 2026 snapshot and as "Technically Complete Application" in an October 30, 2026 snapshot.[2][3]

c04-permit-status.answer: In TCEQ's pending permit list snapshot of 2026-04-10, the Kilby application (permits 181895, GHGPSDTX260, PSDTX1684) was listed as an "Administrative Complete Application."[1] By the 2026-10-30 snapshot, the same row showed the status as a "Technically Complete Application."[2] Both snapshots show the same application date of 10/17/2025, which matches the October 17, 2025 submission date in TCEQ's notice of receipt.[2][1][3] A technical completeness status does not mean final approval: an analyst brief from 2026-07-28 notes the permit is advanced but not equivalent to final authorization.[4]

c02-capacity-change.answer: The air permit application for the Kilby Power Plant was submitted to the TCEQ on October 17, 2025.[1]

c03-turbine-change.answer: The original application, dated October 2025, proposed 17 combustion turbines: 2 GE 7HA.02 combined-cycle turbines, 3 GE 7HA.02 simple-cycle turbines and 12 Solar Titan 350 simple-cycle turbines.[1] In the update to the application, Energy Forge One proposed adding 29 simple-cycle turbines to supply approximately 393 MW of early phase power to meet customer needs.[2] TCEQ's April 10, 2026 summary identifies the added units as Solar Titan 130 turbines that were added on December 22, 2025 and are not intended to remain onsite long-term.[3] After the update, the project scope listed 46 turbines: 2 combined-cycle turbines and 44 simple-cycle turbines, with a nominal capacity of approximately 2,869 MW.[3]

c01-battery-change.answer: The battery storage portion of Project Kilby is listed in the ERCOT queue as "Kilby1 Part 2 Tier1 BESS" (INR 28INR0457), with Energy Forge One LLC as the interconnecting entity.[1] In the June 2026 ERCOT report, this battery project was listed at 560 MW.[2] In the October 2026 ERCOT report, the same project was listed at 330 MW, so its listed size went down between the two reports.[1] Its projected commercial operation date stayed at 2028-01-21 in both reports.[1][2] The "Quantum Storage" battery project in the same reports is a separate Haskell County project at Kilby Switching Station, not part of Project Kilby.[1]

u01-turbine-cost.answer: The provided pages do not give a cost for the GE Vernova turbines. The only dollar figure is National Grid Ventures' $1.75 billion investment for a 35% stake in Joulent, which is not a turbine price.

u05-acreage.answer: The provided pages do not state the acreage of the Kilby site. They give its location in Reeves County, about 20 miles (32.3 km) south of Pecos, and say the area map shows 3,000 feet from the property line, but no site size in acres.

u03-construction-cost.answer: The provided pages do not state a total construction cost for the Kilby power plant. u01-turbine-cost.answer: The provided pages do not give a cost for the GE Vernova turbines. They describe the turbine models and outputs, mention that Engine No. 1's founder procured four gigawatts of GE Vernova gas turbines, and say critical equipment including GE Vernova turbines was secured. None of them states a price. A related-article headline mentions a "$7B Texas power plant," but that refers to the plant, not the turbines.

c06-part6-technology.answer: Yes, the technology listed for Kilby1 Part 6 Large Block Combined Cycle (INR 29INR0199) differs between the two ERCOT interconnection status reports.[1][2] The August 2026 report, published 2026-09-01, lists the technology as CC (combined cycle).[1] The October 2026 report, published 2026-11-02, lists it as GT instead, while the capacity of 1056 MW and the projected COD of 2029-07-19 stay the same.[2] The reports do not explain the change, and the project name still describes it as a combined cycle.[2]

c05-solar-fate.answer: The solar piece of Project Kilby, listed as "Kilby1 Part 5 Solar" (INR 28INR0460) in Reeves County, was cancelled in the ERCOT interconnection queue with a cancel date of 2026-07-06.[1] That cancelled solar entry was sized at 500 MW.[1] The October 2026 ERCOT report still lists other Energy Forge One LLC Kilby1 entries, including Part 1 gas simple cycle, Part 2 battery storage, Part 4 gas simple cycle and Part 6 gas combined cycle, but no Part 5 solar.[2] The "Quantum Solar" project in that report is a separate Haskell County project connecting at a "Kilby Station" and is not part of Project Kilby, and the "Solar T350" units in the air permit are gas-fired combustion turbines, not solar generation.[2][3]

u02-epc-contractor.answer: The provided pages do not name the EPC contractor for Project Kilby. A Latitude Media article published 2026-07-10 says Joulent "hasn't announced the EPC contractor for its Kilby project yet" and was finalizing a contract with "a brand name." The TCEQ filings mention an EPC contractor only in general terms, in connection with the commissioning phase, and do not identify a company. The Frontier Grid brief (2026-07-28) describes equipment and EPC as "advanced by company statement" but also names no contractor.

u05-acreage.answer: The provided pages do not state the site's acreage. They give its location in Reeves County, about 20 miles (32.3 km) south of Pecos, along with driving directions and a list of planned emission sources. None of them gives the size of the site in acres.

u04-ppa-price.answer: The pages describe a 20-year power purchase agreement between Energy Forge One LLC (Chevron) and Microsoft for about 2.67 GW, but none of them state the price per MWh Microsoft will pay. Chevron says only that the project is 'targeting mid-teen returns.' The Frontier Grid brief gives its own gas fuel-price assumptions ($3, $6 and $10/MMBtu), but these are analytical model inputs, not PPA contract terms.

u06-lcoe.answer: The provided pages do not give a levelized cost of electricity for the Kilby Power Plant. They include a carbon capture cost analysis (for example, a final estimate of $194/ton of CO2 removed using 2024 numbers) and Chevron's statement that it can deliver power 'at a competitive cost,' but no levelized cost of electricity figure.

u03-construction-cost.answer: The provided pages do not state a total construction cost for the Kilby power plant. The TCEQ file gives a hypothetical carbon capture cost estimate ($11972 million for capture), which is part of the emissions-control analysis and not the plant's construction cost. The Energy Capital HTX page only includes a linked headline, 'Chevron eyes $7B Texas power plant for Microsoft data center campus', with no article text confirming that figure is Project Kilby's construction cost.

u07-mercuria.answer: The provided pages do not mention Mercuria, a Pecos Power Plant built by Mercuria, or a Texas Energy Fund loan. They cover only Project Kilby (Energy Forge One LLC near Pecos, Reeves County), which is a different project. Its permitted capacity of approximately 2,869 MW should not be attributed to any Mercuria plant.

u10-revenue.answer: The provided pages do not state the annual revenue the Kilby plant will earn from Microsoft. They describe a 20-year power purchase agreement for about 2.67 gigawatts, and Chevron says the project is targeting mid-teen returns. No contract price or revenue figure is given.

u08-engine-no1-price.answer: The provided pages do not say how much Chevron paid Engine No. 1 for any share of Project Kilby. They describe Kilby as a 50-50 joint venture between Chevron and Joulent, which spun out of Engine No. 1. The only investment figure given is National Grid Ventures' $1.75 billion for a 35% stake in Joulent, and that is not a payment by Chevron.

u09-dc-contractor.answer: The provided pages do not name a general contractor for Microsoft's Pecos data center. They only discuss the power plant's EPC contractor: Latitude Media (July 10, 2026) reports that Joulent had not yet announced the EPC contractor for Kilby but was finalizing a contract with 'a brand name.' A Frontier Grid brief says National Grid describes EPC capacity as reserved. Neither identifies a contractor for the data center itself.

h02-7ha-simple-rating.answer: The Kilby Power Plant includes three GE 7HA.02 simple-cycle turbines, and each one is rated at a net output of 330.3 MW.[1][2] These simple-cycle units are proposed to run 8,760 hours per year as base load units and will not be connected to the grid.[2]

h01-t350-rating.answer: Each of the 12 Solar Titan 350 (T350) simple-cycle turbines at the Kilby Power Plant has a net output of 31.1 MW, according to TCEQ's technical review.[1][2] The company's December 22, 2025 response to TCEQ gives the same figure, saying each has an output of 31.1 MW.[3] The figure is stated for site conditions of 59°F inlet air temperature, 60% relative humidity, 2,850 feet elevation and 13.25 psi atmospheric pressure.[3]

h03-early-phase-total.answer: The 29 early-phase simple-cycle turbines have a total nominal net output of approximately 393 MW, measured at 59°F inlet air temperature, 60% relative humidity, and 3,000 feet elevation.[1][2] They are Solar Titan 130 units, each with a net output of 13.55 MW.[3] They were added to the project during the December 22, 2025 application update and are meant to supply early-phase power to meet customer needs, not to stay onsite long-term.[3]

h04-applicant-address.answer: The application's contact sheet, which is meant to accompany all notices, lists Energy Forge One's address as 1500 Louisiana St, Houston, TX 77002-7308.[1] The same sheet names Srimonto Ghosh, Vice President, at that address and at (713) 372-3518 as both the main contact to be shown on the permit and the person responsible for publishing notice.[1] The later permit file at technical completeness repeats the same contact sheet with the same Houston address.[2] The June 10, 2026 public meeting notice tells readers to contact Energy Forge One "at the address stated above" or to call Brian Kane, Permitting Lead, at (713) 920-4177, but the address itself is not on the notice page provided.[3]

h05-regional-office.answer: The TCEQ Midland regional office has a copy of the Kilby Power Plant application, which is available there for viewing and copying, along with the TCEQ central office and the Reeves County Library.[1] The application's notification list calls for hard copies to go to the Air Section Manager at the Midland Regional Office, 10 Desta Drive, Suite 350E, Midland, Texas.[2] TCEQ correspondence dated December 8, 2025 was also copied to the Air Section Manager, Region 7 - Midland.[3]

h06-library.answer: According to TCEQ correspondence in the permit file, residents can view the available documents for this permit application at the Reeves County Library, 315 South Oak Street, Pecos, Reeves County, Texas.[1] The TCEQ engineer, Huy Pham, noted that the library should have internet access where people can download and view the PDF files.[2] He gave this advice on Feb 19, 2026, in reply to a resident who had trouble opening the PDFs on an iPad.[3]

h07-psd-number.answer: The Prevention of Significant Deterioration (PSD) permit number for the Kilby Power Plant is PSDTX1684.[1][2] There is also a separate Greenhouse Gas PSD permit, numbered GHGPSDTX260, alongside the main air quality permit 181895.[1][2] All three permit numbers appear together on TCEQ's pending permit list for Energy Forge One LLC's Kilby application.[3]

h08-ghg-number.answer: The greenhouse gas permit number for the Kilby Power Plant is GHGPSDTX260, issued alongside air permit 181895 and PSD permit PSDTX1684.[1][2] TCEQ's pending permit list shows the same three numbers for Energy Forge One LLC's Kilby application.[3] One TCEQ summary form lists the number as "GHGPSDTX260181895," which looks like GHGPSDTX260 run together with 181895 rather than a different permit number.[4]

h09-part6-inr.answer: ERCOT lists the large block combined cycle part of Kilby as INR 29INR0199, named "Kilby1 Part 6 Large Block Combined Cycle," with Energy Forge One LLC as the interconnecting entity in Reeves County.[1][2] Both the August 2026 and October 2026 ERCOT reports show it at 1056 MW with a projected COD of 2029-07-19.[1][2] The two reports differ on the technology code: the August 2026 report lists it as CC, while the October 2026 report lists it as GT.[2][1]

h11-chevron-exec.answer: Chevron's announcement of its power agreement with Microsoft quotes Jeff Gustavson, Chevron's president of New Energies.[1] In that release, Gustavson said Chevron is uniquely positioned to deliver power to customers with certainty, speed and at a competitive cost, leveraging Permian natural gas.[1] E&E News reported the same quote and attributed it to Gustavson.[2]

h12-microsoft-exec.answer: Noelle Walsh, Microsoft president of Cloud Operations + Innovation, is quoted in Chevron's announcement of the agreement.[1] She said the agreement with Chevron helps ensure Microsoft will have dedicated, large-scale power to support the evolution and reliability of advanced compute.[1] She also said that through the partnership, Microsoft is delighted to grow with and become a deeper part of the West Texas community.[1]

h10-part4-mw.answer: Kilby1 Part 4 Large Block Simple Cycle (INR 28INR0457 is a different part; Part 4 is INR 28INR0459), interconnected by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County, is listed in the ERCOT queue at 950 MW in the October 2026 report.[1] The January 2026 ERCOT report showed the same 950 MW capacity for this project, so the figure did not change between the two reports.[2] Both reports list it as a gas turbine project with a projected commercial operation date of 2028-04-20.[1][2]

h13-target-returns.answer: Chevron says Project Kilby is targeting mid-teen returns.[1] Chevron also says the project is expected to generate diversified cash flow that does not depend on oil and gas price cycles, which it says supports resilient shareholder returns.[1] This target comes from Chevron's own June 22, 2026 press release (a company source), which also states that these statements are forward-looking and not guarantees of future performance.[2][3]

h14-nox-tpy.answer: The plain language summary for permit 181895 proposes 886.34 tons per year of NOx for all facilities at the Kilby site combined.[1] The same figure appears in the summary filed with the application and in the later permit file at technical completeness.[2][3] The summary says the turbines' NOx will be controlled by selective catalytic reduction, and it notes that the figures may change during TCEQ's technical review.[1]

h16-solar-cancel-date.answer: ERCOT's July 2026 interconnection status report lists the Kilby1 Part 5 Solar queue entry (INR 28INR0460, 500 MW, Reeves County) with a cancel date of 2026-07-06.[1] The Quantum Solar project that connects at Kilby Station is in Haskell County and is a separate, unrelated project, not part of Project Kilby.[2]

h15-class-i-area.answer: The closest Class I area to the Kilby Power Plant is Carlsbad Caverns National Park, about 150 km to the northwest of the project.[1] The other two Class I areas within 300 km are Guadalupe Mountains National Park at 153 km to the northwest and Big Bend National Park at 160 km to the south.[2] The application states that no PSD Class I areas lie within 100 km of the site.[1]

h19-construction-workforce.answer: None of the provided pages state the number of construction workers expected on site at peak. The pages cover the TCEQ permit notice, dispersion modeling protocol, fuel-supply readiness analysis, and staff biographies, but give no construction workforce figures.

h20-insurance.answer: The provided pages do not describe any insurance coverage for Project Kilby. They cover the 2.67-gigawatt plant announcement, the 20-year power purchase agreement, turbine suppliers, estimated emissions, and gas-supply and pipeline-capacity questions, but say nothing about insurance.

h17-part4-cod.answer: ERCOT lists a projected commercial operation date of 2028-04-20 for Kilby1 Part 4 Large Block Simple Cycle (INR 28INR0459), a 950 MW gas project by Energy Forge One LLC in Reeves County.[1] The date has not moved between the two reports provided: the January 2026 report (published 2026-02-02) also showed 2028-04-20, as does the October 2026 report (published 2026-11-02).[2][1] What did change between the reports is the study status: Part 4's screening study moved from started to completed, with completion dated 2026-02-04.[2][1]

h18-heat-rate.answer: The provided pages do not state a heat rate in Btu per kWh for the Kilby Power Plant as a whole. The closest figures cover only parts of the project or are assumptions. A Caterpillar G3520 engine data sheet (P1) lists genset fuel consumption in Btu/ekW-hr, and Table 29 (P2) ties that engine model to units BSGEN1-BSGEN2. These are individual engine specifications, not the plant's heat rate. The Frontier Grid brief (P7, tier 4 analysis) uses heat rates of 7.0, 8.0 and 9.5 MMBtu/MWh, but only as scenarios for estimating fuel demand, not as a disclosed plant value.

h21-debt-rate.answer: The provided pages do not state an interest rate for any Project Kilby debt. One press page (Latitude Media) says only that lining up project financing is among the last steps before breaking ground, and that it "shouldn't be too hard given the 20-year PPA with Microsoft is already in place." No financing terms, lenders, or rates are given.
